title: DEIM-L vs RT-DETR-R101: benchmark on COCO
dek: DEIM-L leads by 1.0 mAP on under half the parameters, and turns RT-DETR-R101's PyTorch speed lead around once you convert the model.
author: Vision Analysis

blocks.text: DEIM-L is the more accurate detector, 57.8 vs 56.8 mAP@50-95 against RT-DETR-R101 on an RTX 5070 Ti in PyTorch, both at 640 px. RT-DETR-R101 is 21.09% faster there, 23.6 vs 18.6 FPS, but that lead does not survive conversion: DEIM-L is faster on ONNX Runtime, TensorRT FP32, and Jetson Orin. DEIM-L also uses far less VRAM, 245 vs 456 MB, on under half the parameters.
DEIM-L (31.24M parameters) and RT-DETR-R101 (76.56M) both ship under Apache-2.0 and evaluate at 640 px on COCO val2017. Both have verified rows on desktop GPU and Jetson Orin, across three runtimes.

blocks.caption: Accuracy vs parameters on COCO val2017. DEIM-L and RT-DETR-R101 highlighted against the full set.

blocks.text: mAP is shown in percent form. DEIM-L measures 57.8 mAP@50-95 to RT-DETR-R101's 56.8, a 1.0 point lead on under half the parameter count. DEIM-L also leads on small objects: 45.2 vs 39.2 mAP_small, a 15.18% relative gap.

In PyTorch on the RTX 5070 Ti, RT-DETR-R101 runs 23.6 FPS to DEIM-L's 18.6. The order reverses under conversion: DEIM-L reaches 75.7 vs 64.4 FPS on TensorRT FP32 and 50.5 vs 47.5 on ONNX Runtime. DEIM-L extracts 189.95% more mAP per GFLOP.
The PyTorch speed win does not carry to the edge. On Jetson Orin, DEIM-L runs 4.8 FPS to RT-DETR-R101's 2.8.

Pick DEIM-L for most deployments: it is more accurate, faster on converted runtimes and Jetson, and uses less than half the VRAM at 245 vs 456 MB. Pick RT-DETR-R101 when PyTorch throughput is the one metric that matters. Both ship under Apache-2.0.

# pip install libreyolo
from libreyolo import LibreYOLO

deim = LibreYOLO("LibreDEIMl.pt")         # 31.24M params, 57.8 mAP@50-95
rtdetr = LibreYOLO("LibreRTDETRr101.pt")  # 76.56M params, 56.8 mAP@50-95

results = deim("image.jpg")
